questions.q: What is 'Create Invoice in Spreadsheet' used for?
options: Creating new Payables invoices directly through a connected ADFdi Excel workbook, without going through FBDI
Purging rejected interface rows
Generating CSV files for FBDI templates
Installing the ADFdi Excel add-in
questions.explain: Create Invoice in Spreadsheet is an ADFdi action used to create new invoices directly in a connected spreadsheet, bypassing the FBDI pipeline entirely.

questions.q: Why does Create Invoice in Spreadsheet have both header fields and line fields, just like the FBDI Payables Invoice Import template?
options: Pure coincidence with no underlying reason
Because an invoice itself has two levels — header and line — and that business shape doesn't change based on which tool is used to load it
Because ADFdi requires exactly two sections in every spreadsheet
Because line fields are optional and rarely used
questions.explain: The header/line structure reflects the actual shape of an invoice as a business object, not a quirk of either specific loading tool.

questions.q: What do Correct Import Errors (from Chapter 5) and Create Invoice in Spreadsheet have in common?
options: Nothing — they are built on completely unrelated technologies
Both require a ZIP file to be uploaded to UCM
Both are built on the same underlying ADFdi technology, just used for two different jobs — correcting failed FBDI rows versus creating new invoices directly
Both can only be used by Oracle employees
questions.explain: This lesson highlights that ADFdi is a general capability used for multiple purposes — error correction in one context, direct invoice creation in another.

questions.q: Which scenario is the best fit for Create Invoice in Spreadsheet rather than FBDI?
options: A nightly file of 3,000 invoices from a supplier portal
A recurring, unattended system-to-system feed
A one-time conversion of 40,000 legacy invoices at go-live
A handful of invoices that arrived by email this week, with no batch file involved
questions.explain: A small, ad-hoc batch with no existing file is exactly the scale ADFdi suits — fast setup and immediate feedback, without FBDI's full pipeline.

questions.q: What determines whether FBDI or ADFdi is the better choice for a given Payables invoice loading task?
options: The same volume, frequency, and 'who is doing the work' factors introduced in lesson 1
The user's personal preference alone
Whichever tool was used most recently
The color scheme of the Excel workbook
questions.explain: The decision framework from lesson 1 — volume, frequency, and who performs the work — applies consistently across every module in this course, including this comparison.
